images.title: Bigger base, smaller power
images.purpose: Shows the cards 4³ and 3⁴ with bars of 64 and 81 from one baseline, so 3⁴ is larger.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two cards side by side, each with a horizontal bar beneath, both bars starting at one left edge.
images.exact_structure: Two equal white cards side by side: the left card reads 4³ with a teal (#0072B2) outline, the right card reads 3⁴ with a reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline. Below them, two horizontal bars that start at the same vertical baseline at the left: a teal bar of length 64 units labelled 64 at its end, and under it a reddish purple bar of length 81 units labelled 81 at its end, so the second bar is about one quarter longer. Under the bars the label 3⁴ is larger. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A bigger base does not always give a bigger power: 3⁴ = 81 beats 4³ = 64.
images.description: Shows the cards 4³ and 3⁴ with bars of 64 and 81 from one baseline, so 3⁴ is larger.

image_decisions.why: The practice tool's core move is comparing two power cards with bars from one origin; this is its simplest duel.
